proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions are driven by a distinct severity/hospitalization process rather than a lagged infection proxy, delayed_I may mis-time peaks or misrepresent tail behavior.
proposals.rationale: Hospitalization-rate target can plausibly reflect infections with a short reporting/admission lag; SEIRS captures waning immunity across a season while remaining parsimonious for a 31-week training window and moderate peakiness.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-long lag can shift peaks too far right and degrade short-horizon forecasts when the true lag is shorter or time-varying.
proposals.rationale: A slightly longer lag can better align observed hospitalizations with upstream transmission dynamics when admission occurs several weeks after exposure; SEIRS supports recurrent susceptibility without adding an explicit hospitalization state.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H dynamics may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter confounding (e.g., I→H vs recovery) and unstable forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the hospitalization-rate target to an explicit H compartment, matching surveillance semantics and allowing separation between infectious prevalence and admissions when identifiable.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target is truly admissions-only, mixing I with H can bias level/shape and inflate peaks, reducing interpretability and calibration.
proposals.rationale: If reported hospitalization rates reflect a mixture of current severe infections and admissions (or if the signal correlates with both), observing I+H can provide robustness when H alone is noisy or under-identified.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If reinfection/waning materially affects late-season dynamics, SEIR may underfit the tail or misrepresent secondary rises.
proposals.rationale: A more parsimonious alternative to SEIRS when waning immunity is not strongly expressed within the observed window; delayed_I retains the key hospitalization-lag mechanism while reducing state complexity.
